Fires on the verb (or head noun) of clauses about a thing performing/serving its function — e.g. "work" in "doesn't seem to work", "provide" after "the value that vouchers", "can"/"do" in "it can be flipped"/"can do double duty", "system" in "air conditioning system", "it" in "does what it needs to do" — i.e., the token right where the functioning/utility predicate is stated, usually just after a subject pronoun/relative clause.

L7·N5038unmasked layer
Fires on the token that completes a multi-token lexical unit near the start of a passage — the final syllable of a surname/proper name (Gross**man**, McClus**key**, Ether **Capital**) or the closing word of a fixed collocation/idiom ("at **best**", "Chances **are**", "can't stand **it**") — and is suppressed on ordinary mid-sentence function words like "the"/"She".
